titleEn: A Gap in the Curtain, a Strip of Light!

pages.text: The curtains slid shut, dimming the classroom. "Lala, lie on your mat." Teacher Bau of Rainbow Class spread a blanket. Timid Lala stopped before the mat.
Lala wanted to lie down too, but looking toward the dark made those shoulders hunch. "In the dark, I cannot see what is there." Lala covered both ears.
A big pointed thing stood by the wall. To Lala, it looked scary. "What... is that?" Lala stepped back.
The children already slept peacefully. On the next mat, careless Duri slept with a hand outside. Only Lala sat hugging their knees. Half of nap time had passed.
Teacher Bau sat facing Lala across the mat. "Lala, what scared you?" Lala pointed toward the wall.

Teacher Bau moved the curtain edge slightly. A strip of light slipped in, crossing the wall. The pointed thing was a raincoat on a hook, with boots side by side below. "A gap in the curtain, a strip of light! Now we can see it all."
This time, Lala moved the curtain. Light crossed a box in the corner. The round thing was a toy pot. Looking at things one by one left nothing scary. "A gap in the curtain, a strip of light!"
Lala lay on the mat. Duri's hand was still outside. Lala held it tightly. A long strip of curtain light lay between them.

Teacher Bau whispered three things in Lala's ear. "One, say you are scared! Two, a gap in the curtain, a strip of light! Three, hold the hand beside you!" When the curtain closed again, Lala parted it with a finger.

Teacher Bau pulled the blanket to Lala's neck and stroked their back. "Dark just means the curtain is hiding the light." Even in darkness, one strip of light showed what things were. Closing their eyes, Lala murmured sleepily, "A gap in the curtain... a strip of light..."
